newsitem.title: USA: "101 Dalmatians" sends Disney earnings higher.
newsitem.headline: "101 Dalmatians" sends Disney earnings higher.

text.p: Strong box office sales for "101 Dalmatians" and record attendance at Walt Disney Co.'s theme parks added up to better-than-expected quarterly profits, the company said Tuesday.

The Burbank, Calif.-based entertainment giant reported a profit of $749 million, or $1.09 a share, in its fiscal first quarter ended in December, up 51 percent from the $496 million or 93 cents a share reported a year ago. Revenues rose 64 percent to $6.3 billion.

"Walt Disney World led the way in our theme park division and the impressive box office performance of our holiday movies and home video releases also contributed to the company's results," said Michael Eisner, Disney chairman. "Worldwide merchandise licensing and ESPN continue to show strong growth and were significant factors in the company's overall performance."

Disney's results were aided by a one-time gain of $135 million on the sale of Los Angeles television station KCAL and reductions in amortization costs related to Disney's $19 billion acquisition of Capital Cities/ABC Inc. last year.
However, even without the benefits, industry analysts said Disney had a strong quarter, particularly at its theme parks.
"The theme parks were unbelievable," said Jessica Reif, with Merrill Lynch in New York. "Attendance was up probably the highest it's been that I can remember in a quarter."

She said attendance was up an estimated 10 percent across the board with most of the gains coming from Disney World in Florida. In addition, Reif said theme park guest spending was higher in the quarter and hotel occupancy rates were above 90 percent.
Disney said revenue from theme parks and resorts rose 16 percent to $1.2 billion for the quarter and operating income jumped 21 percent.
On a proforma basis, which assumes Disney had owned ABC in the year-ago quarter, net income rose 33 percent for the quarter and revenues rose 7 percent.
Excluding the gain from KCAL, Disney reported earnings per share of 98 cents, better than the First Call consensus estimate of 94 cents. On Wall Street, Disney stock jumped $2 to $73.625.

Analysts attributed the stock rise to the strong financial results, Disney's decision to buy a majority stake in cable channel E! Entertainment Television with partner Comcast Corp. and Disney's announcement that it might sell the publishing operations it acquired from ABC.

According to people familiar with the Comcast deal, Disney has agreed to put up about $320 million to acquire Time Warner Inc.'s stake in the popular cable channel. Together Disney and Comcast would own 70 percent of E! Entertainment.
Reif said the move was a cheap way for Disney to acquire another cable channel when access to subscribers is commanding hefty premiums.
"They're paying roughly $12 to $13 per subscriber," she said. "New networks are offering more than that just to get on and this is a profitable network."

Disney also said it would begin reviewing its options for the publishing operations it acquired as part of the ABC acquisition. The unit includes the printing and distribution of daily and weekly newspapers, specialised publications for various industries, and consumer, special interest and agricultural publications.
Jeff Logsdon, analyst at Cruttendon, Roth said the operations could fetch as much as $2.5 billion in an auction.

"From Disney's standpoint, I think there are very little obvious synergistic benefits to these assets," he said, noting it was unlikely publications like "Women's Wear Daily" and "Institutional Investor" could fit into Disney's strategy of exploiting the Mickey Mouse brand around the world.

On the film side, Disney credited its re-make of "101 Dalmatians," the international release of "the Hunchback of Notre Dame," and other movies such as "The English Patient" for the division's strong performance.

Disney said its Creative Content division, which includes studios, consumer products and the former ABC publishing operations generated $3.24 billion in revenues for the quarter, up 5 percent, and operating income of $719 million, up 10 percent.

The Broadcasting division, which includes television and radio stations and cable channels such as ESPN and the Disney Channel, generated first quarter revenues of $1.89 billion, up 4 percent, and operating income of $470 million, up 38 percent.
On Monday, Disney announced it would increase its quarterly dividend to 13.25 cents per share from 11 cents.
